Hi Samir / Emily —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before scheduling an initial benchmark run: 

Call recap:
- Goal: validate Redwood Dedicated can meet EdgeFin production SLOs for low-latency streaming and high-concurrency inference for your risk-scoring model.
- Primary SLOs you called out: P95 latency for first streaming token and for full-response, throughput targets for batch scoring, and concurrency scale to ~12 concurrent live sessions.

What we need from you to kick off the benchmark:
1) Your canonical prompt set / sample traffic (examples + distribution).
2) Target SLOs (P50/P95/P99) for both "streaming start" and "end-to-end" generation.
3) Typical payload size (context length, output tokens) and concurrency expectations (baseline and peak).
4) Any disallowed behaviors or redlines (privacy, redaction needs).

If you can send the prompt set and a short note on the SLO numbers, I’ll loop in our solutions team and we’ll propose a reproducible methodology and schedule a 48–72h window to run the tests.

Proposed next step: Samir to send prompt set + SLOs by EOD Wed; Redwood to share harness + measurement spec and propose Wed/Thu next-week test window.

Thanks —

Marissa — thanks for the quick recap. 

Attaching our prompt set (edgefin_prompt_set_v1.json) which contains ~1200 anonymized examples across the 3 scoring flows. A few clarifications on SLOs and traffic: 
- Target SLOs (production):
  - Streaming start (time-to-first-byte): P95 <= 200ms
  - Full-response generation (end-to-end): P95 <= 350ms for the typical 512-token response distribution
  - P99 targets are less strict but we expect P99 < 700ms for critical flows
- Concurrency: baseline 8 concurrent sessions, peak 24 concurrent sessions during market open bursts.
- Throughput: batch scoring jobs are ~5k requests/hour during nightly runs; per-request latency is more important for live sessions.

We can provide a test API key and a small test corpus. I redacted the real keys in the file but included placeholders (edgefin_test_keys_redacted.txt) — we will provide temp credentials when we confirm the slot.

Happy to run in the week of Aug 10; prefer Wed/Thu afternoon PST.

—Samir

Subject: Benchmark harness + methodology (draft)

Hi Samir / team —

Thanks for sending the prompt set and targets. Attached is our harness bundle (redwood_benchmark_harness_v3.tar.gz) and a short methodology summary below. I included a Drive folder with scripts and a reproducibility checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e6f

High-level methodology (draft) — please review and flag anything non-representative: 
1) Environment
   - Dedicated cluster: 4xA100 (80GB) nodes reserved for the run (we'll provide instance details ahead of time).
   - Model variant: open-model v2.1 quantized FP16 with Redwood runtime kernels.
2) Warmup vs measurement
   - Warmup: 60 minutes of traffic to populate KV cache, run the same distribution as the prompt_set at 50% of baseline concurrency.
   - Measurement window: 30 minutes steady-state followed by 30 minutes stepped-load (baseline -> peak) to capture P50/P95/P99 and tail behavior.
3) Definitions
   - Streaming start latency: time from request sunrise (socket send) to first data chunk received by client.
   - End-to-end latency: time from request send to last byte of response received.
   - We will capture client-side and server-side timestamps and include request IDs for traceability.
4) Concurrency shaping
   - Baseline: 8 concurrent long-running sessions (average session length 18s).
   - Peak: step to 24 concurrent sessions for 10 minutes during measurement window.
5) Caching and determinism
   - Prefix caching will be enabled to reflect production; we will run a cold-run baseline without cache for comparison.
6) Reproducibility artifacts
   - We will deliver: harness scripts, seed values, raw trace logs (request ids), and a results workbook (benchmark_results_template.xlsx).

Questions for EdgeFin: 
- Do you have any additional compliance or data-retention constraints for the logs we generate?
- For end-to-end measurements, do you prefer client-side or server-side latency be the canonical metric for SLAs? We recommend client-side P95 for production-facing guarantees.

If that looks good I'll finalize the harness and share the exact cluster specs + temp credentials for the test.

- Monica
Monica Patel
